editorial:
If you have ever rooted for the underdog, this animated adventure gives you a hunchbacked hero worth cheering for. Igor is tired of being the sidekick who just pulls the switch for his evil boss. He wants to invent something amazing himself, even if the whole evil science world laughs at him. The movie mixes spooky castle vibes with bright, colorful animation, so it feels like a Halloween party that never gets too scary. Kids will giggle at the silly monsters, while adults will catch the jokes about ambition and fitting in.

The voice cast brings real energy and makes Igor feel lovable. The pacing moves quickly, jumping from one wild invention to the next, though some jokes land better than others. On the downside, the story follows a pretty familiar path, and a few side characters feel underused. Still, the heart shines through, and the final act delivers a satisfying payoff. Families with older kids will have a blast, and animation fans should give it a shot. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your shelf.
endingExplained: Igor finally creates Eva, a giant monster meant to win the evil science fair, but she turns out kind and gentle instead of scary. When the evil scientist Dr. Schadenfreude steals Igor's work, Igor refuses to give up. In the finale, Eva saves the day by using her strength for good, and Igor exposes the truth about the evil science community. Igor is finally recognized as a real scientist, and the town learns that kindness beats cruelty.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated underdog stories and spooky-but-silly family fun.
